# Haalendar API reference

<!-- Generated from api/openapi.yaml by backend/tests/api_reference.py: do not edit by hand. After a change of the contract, run `cd backend && uv run python -m tests.api_reference`. -->

Haalendar API 1.1.0: Calendar, To-Do and Kanban — self-hosted, multi-user, offline-first. The contract is [`api/openapi.yaml`](../../api/openapi.yaml) (OpenAPI 3.1); this page is written from it, and a test fails when the two differ. How to call the API from a script: [api-usage.md](api-usage.md).

Base path: `/api/v1`, on the address of the installation. 122 operations, 66 of them served by the server; the others are described for completeness and say how their data is reached instead (most through offline sync).

## Conventions

- JSON with snake_case fields; IDs are UUIDv7 and may be generated by clients (offline creation).
- Errors: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.
- Updates: `PATCH` with `application/merge-patch+json` (RFC 7396) and `If-Match: "<version>"`.
- Deletes are always soft; responses carry `delete_batch_id` for restore.
- Lists: cursor pagination (`cursor`, `limit`, `next_cursor`).
- Unsafe requests: session cookie + `X-CSRF-Token`; optional `Idempotency-Key`.

More, with the error codes and the rate limits: [`api/README.md`](../../api/README.md).

## Authentication

| Scheme | Where | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| sessionCookie | cookie | `__Host-haalendar_session` | Opaque server-side session (ADR-0005). HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. |
| csrfToken | header | `X-CSRF-Token` | Required on every unsafe method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) together with the session cookie. |

Operations marked **Public** need neither.

- [setup](#tag-setup) — First-run wizard (2)
- [auth](#tag-auth) — Login, registration, password reset, re-authentication, OIDC (12)

- [admin](#tag-admin) — Account administration (no content access) (8)

## setup

<a id="tag-setup"></a>

First-run wizard

### GET /setup/status

<a id="op-getsetupstatus"></a>

Whether the first-run admin wizard is still required

- **Public:** no sign-in needed.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Setup state | `application/json`, below |

Body of `200`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setup_required` | boolean | yes |  |
| `setup_token_required` | boolean | yes | HAALENDAR_SETUP_TOKEN must be entered (always in production) |
| `registration_mode` | string: `invite`, `open` | yes |  |
| `demo_mode` | boolean | yes |  |

### POST /setup/admin

<a id="op-createfirstadmin"></a>

Create the first admin (only while setup is required) and sign in — FR-ACC-05

- **Public:** no sign-in needed.

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string (email) | yes | max length `254` |
| `password` | [NewPassword](#schema-newpassword) | yes |  |
| `display_name` | string | yes | min length `1`, max length `80` |
| `time_zone` | [TimeZone](#schema-timezone) | yes |  |
| `setup_token` | string |  | Required when setup_token_required; max length `256` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | Admin created and logged in (session cookie set) | `application/json` [Me](#schema-me) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | State conflict (`duplicate`, `invalid_state`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### PUT /me/avatar

<a id="op-uploadavatar"></a>

Upload avatar image (PNG/JPEG/WebP, ≤ 2 MB, raw body); returns the updated profile

The file itself is the request body. The declared Content-Type must be one of the image types, but only the file signature decides; anything else is refused with 415. Images over 40 megapixels are refused with 413.

**Request body** `image/png`

Type: string

**Request body** `image/jpeg`

Type: string

**Request body** `image/webp`

Type: string

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Avatar replaced | `application/json` [Me](#schema-me) |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 413 | Body or file exceeds the limit (`payload_too_large`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 415 | Content type not accepted (`unsupported_media_type`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### DELETE /me/avatar

<a id="op-removeavatar"></a>

Remove the avatar from the profile (the stored file is kept, never deleted)

- **Soft delete:** The profile stops referencing the image; the stored file is kept.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Avatar removed | `application/json` [Me](#schema-me) |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /me/push-subscriptions

<a id="op-addpushsubscription"></a>

Register a Web Push subscription for this device (FR-CAL-29)

The browser's PushSubscription (toJSON). The same endpoint again refreshes the user's subscription; other users' active subscriptions of the endpoint (a shared browser) are revoked. Production accepts only https endpoints of the known push services (Google, Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple, plus configured hosts); others are 422.

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string (uri) | yes | max length `2048` |
| `keys` | object | yes |  |
| `keys.p256dh` | string | yes |  |
| `keys.auth` | string | yes |  |
| `expirationTime` | integer or null |  | Sent by browsers; not used |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | Registered | `application/json`, below |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `201`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  |  |

### POST /admin/invites

<a id="op-admininviteuser"></a>

Invite a user by e-mail; without SMTP creates the account with a one-time password instead (requires re-auth)

With SMTP an invitation link (valid 7 days) is e-mailed; a new invitation for the same address revokes the previous one, so repeating the request is safe. Without SMTP the account is created immediately (e-mail treated as verified) and a one-time password is returned once; it must be changed at the first login. The `Idempotency-Key` header is accepted; generic replay handling arrives with offline sync.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUID. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response; same key with a different body → 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are kept 24 h |

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string (email) | yes | max length `254` |
| `role` | string: `admin`, `user` |  | default `user` |
| `display_name` | string |  | Used for the account created without SMTP; default: local part of the e-mail; min length `1`, max length `80` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | Invite created | `application/json`, below |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | State conflict (`duplicate`, `invalid_state`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `201`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delivery` | string: `email`, `one_time_password` | yes |  |
| `invite` | [AdminInvite](#schema-admininvite) |  |  |
| `user` | [AdminUser](#schema-adminuser) |  |  |
| `one_time_password` | string |  | Only when SMTP is not configured; shown once |

### POST /items/{id}/attachments

<a id="op-uploadattachment"></a>

Upload an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF ≤ 10 MB, type verified by content) — FR-X-11

The file signature decides the type (the declared Content-Type must still be one of the four). PNG, JPEG and still WebP are decoded and written anew without metadata (EXIF/GPS); animated GIF and WebP are kept as sent after validation. Limits: 10 MB, 40 megapixels, 300 frames, 20 attachments per item. A thumbnail (WebP, at most 320 px) is created at once. Needs edit access to the item's container.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUID. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response; same key with a different body → 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are kept 24 h |
| `X-File-Name` | header | string | yes | Original file name, percent-encoded UTF-8; min length `1`, max length `1024` |
| `X-Attachment-Id` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUIDv7 (offline creation) |

**Request body** `image/png`

Type: string

**Request body** `image/jpeg`

Type: string

**Request body** `image/webp`

Type: string

**Request body** `image/gif`

Type: string

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | Stored | `application/json` [Attachment](#schema-attachment) |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 404 | Resource does not exist or is not visible to the user (no existence leak). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | State conflict (`duplicate`, `invalid_state`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 413 | Body or file exceeds the limit (`payload_too_large`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 415 | Content type not accepted (`unsupported_media_type`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /items/{id}/convert

<a id="op-convertitem"></a>

Convert note ↔ card ↔ event keeping content, attachments and links (FR-INT-02)

The item becomes another kind in place: the same id, so its links, attachments (the same files) and history stay. The title, description, colour and priority are kept; an event's start becomes a due date and back (a due date without a time makes an all-day event, with a time an event of one hour; none makes it fall on `start_date`, by default today in the user's zone); an event's place goes to the top of the description; a checklist stays between notes and cards and becomes a Markdown list in an event's description. What the new kind has no place for — labels without a label of the same name where it goes, the assignees and comments of a card, the checklist rows of an event, the user's own reminders of another form — is soft-deleted in one batch, answered as `batch_id`. Undo converts back with `undo` set to that batch: the item takes its earlier place and details again (the ones it had there), `title` and `body` as given, and what the batch took comes back. Write access is needed where the item is and where it goes; only the owner's own items become notes, a shared note is not converted, nor a repeating event or a changed occurrence of one. Needs a connection. Converting to the kind it already is answers the item as it is.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUID. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response; same key with a different body → 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are kept 24 h |

**Request body** `application/json`

Type: [ConvertItem](#schema-convertitem)

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Converted | `application/json` [ConvertedItem](#schema-converteditem) |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 404 | Resource does not exist or is not visible to the user (no existence leak). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | State conflict (`duplicate`, `invalid_state`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /shares

<a id="op-createshare"></a>

Share a container with another user of the instance (owner only)

422 with an error on /grantee_email when no active user has that address (code user_not_found) or it is the owner's own address (code self); on /container_kind when the kind is not available yet (code unsupported). 404 when the container is not visible, 403 when it is visible but not owned. 409 duplicate when the user already has access (change the permission instead). The Idempotency-Key header is accepted; generic replay handling arrives with offline sync.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUID. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response; same key with a different body → 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are kept 24 h |

| `container_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `grantee_email` | string (email) | yes | max length `254` |
| `permission` | [Permission](#schema-permission) | yes |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | Shared | `application/json` [Share](#schema-share) |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 404 | Resource does not exist or is not visible to the user (no existence leak). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | State conflict (`duplicate`, `invalid_state`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /trash/restore

<a id="op-restorefromtrash"></a>

Restore entries (with children of the same delete batch) to their original place

Each entry brings back its whole delete batch. Entries that cannot be restored are reported in `failed` (codes: not_found — unknown, already restored or not visible; forbidden — visible but not yours to restore; unsupported — type not available yet; parent_in_trash — its container is in the trash too: restore `parent` first or together).

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entries` | array of object | yes | min items `1`, max items `500` |
| `entries[].type` | string: `event`, `note`, `card`, `calendar`, `board`, `column`, `attachment`, `checklist_item`, `comment`, `label`, `link`, `reminder` | yes |  |
| `entries[].id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Restored entries | `application/json`, below |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `200`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `restored` | integer | yes | Entries restored |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Records brought back, children of the batches included |
| `failed` | array of object | yes |  |
| `failed[].type` | string | yes |  |
| `failed[].id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `failed[].code` | string: `not_found`, `forbidden`, `unsupported`, `parent_in_trash` | yes |  |
| `failed[].parent` | object or null |  |  |

### POST /exports

<a id="op-requestexport"></a>

Request a data export of the chosen modules (FR-X-14); needs a recent password confirmation

Exports what the user owns: the containers they own and everything in them, soft-deleted records included with deleted_at. One export at a time (409 invalid_state while one is queued or running). The archive is built in the background; poll listExports (an e-mail is sent when mail is configured).

## bulk

<a id="tag-bulk"></a>

Multi-select operations

### POST /bulk

<a id="op-bulkoperation"></a>

Apply one action to many items atomically — one undo step (FR-X-07)

All-or-nothing: when any target cannot be changed nothing is changed, and the problem lists the offending targets as errors with pointer /targets/{index} and a code (not_found, forbidden, version_conflict, unsupported, invalid_state). Only version conflicts → 412 version_conflict; otherwise 422 validation_failed. delete removes all targets in one delete batch; restore brings back the delete batch of each target. A repeated request after success fails with version_conflict (versions have moved on), so retrying with the same Idempotency-Key never applies twice.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) |  | Client-generated UUID. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response; same key with a different body → 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are kept 24 h |

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string: `delete`, `restore`, `set_color`, `set_priority` | yes |  |
| `targets` | array of [BulkTarget](#schema-bulktarget) | yes | min items `1`, max items `500` |
| `color` | [Color](#schema-color) |  | set_color — value for targets without their own color |
| `priority` | [Priority](#schema-priority) |  | set_priority — value for targets without their own priority |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | All applied (all-or-nothing) | `application/json`, below |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 412 | `If-Match` does not match the current version (`version_conflict`); body contains the current resource in `current`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `200`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applied` | integer | yes |  |
| `delete_batch_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) or null | yes |  |
| `items` | array of [BulkItemResult](#schema-bulkitemresult) | yes | Every changed row with its new version (rows restored together with a target are not listed) |

## sync

<a id="tag-sync"></a>

Offline sync (ADR-0009): pull, push and the live event stream

### GET /sync/pull

<a id="op-syncpull"></a>

Changes visible to the user since a cursor (including soft deletes and revoked-share tombstones)

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | query | string |  | Opaque cursor (last sync_seq handed out plus the transactions still in progress then, ADR-0009); omit for the initial sync; max length `4096` |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | min `1`, max `1000`, default `500` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Change batch | `application/json`, below |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 410 | Cursor unknown, too old or of another database (restored from a backup): start over with a full sync | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `200`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changes` | array of [Change](#schema-change) | yes |  |
| `cursor` | string | yes |  |
| `has_more` | boolean | yes |  |

### POST /sync/push

<a id="op-syncpush"></a>

Apply queued offline mutations in order; each mutation is idempotent by its id

Each mutation runs through the same service code as the regular endpoints (authorisation, validation, audit, soft delete) in its own transaction; a failure does not stop the batch. A repeated mutation_id answers duplicate with the stored result. Conflicts follow ADR-0009: disjoint fields merge, the same field changed elsewhere answers conflict with the server state.

**Request body** `application/json`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mutations` | array of [Mutation](#schema-mutation) | yes | min items `1`, max items `500` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Per-mutation results | `application/json`, below |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Body is well-formed but invalid (`validation_failed`); see `errors`. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Body of `200`:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `results` | array of object | yes |  |
| `results[].mutation_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `results[].status` | string: `applied`, `duplicate`, `conflict`, `rejected` | yes | rejected = validation, permission or not found; never retried |
| `results[].version` | integer |  | New version when applied |
| `results[].fields` | array of string |  | Conflicting fields |
| `results[].problem` | [Problem](#schema-problem) |  |  |
| `results[].current` | object |  | Server state on conflict, and on rejected when the record was deleted on another device |
| `results[].edited_elsewhere` | boolean |  | delete: applied, but the record had been changed since base_version (it can be restored from the trash) |

### GET /stream

<a id="op-openeventstream"></a>

Server-Sent Events with change notifications for open sessions (no per-second polling)

Session cookie. The first event is `changes`. Events: `changes` (run a sync pull), `notification` (a new notification), `ping` (every 25 s; the session is checked then — a revoked or expired session ends the stream, the reconnect gets 401). Data is always `{}`. `retry: 5000`. At most 10 streams per user.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | text/event-stream; events: `changes`, `notification`, `ping` (data `{}`); `demo_reset` is reserved for the demo mode | `text/event-stream` string |
| 401 | Not authenticated or session expired (`session_expired`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed (`forbidden`, `csrf_failed`, `reauth_required`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Rate limit or temporary account lock (`rate_limited`, `account_locked`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### Change

<a id="schema-change"></a>

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity_type` | string: `calendar`, `share`, `item`, `attachment`, `settings`, `reminder`, `checklist_item`, `board`, `board_column`, `label`, `item_label`, `card_assignee`, `link`, `comment`, `note` | yes | Resource; for a tombstone the container kind. reminder: the user's own reminders (HAAL-091, D-79); checklist_item: the items of the notes the user reads (HAAL-101, D-88); board: the boards the user owns or that are shared with them (HAAL-110, D-90); board_column: the columns of the boards the user reads (HAAL-111, D-91); label, item_label: the labels of those boards and the labels on their cards (HAAL-112, D-92), and the user's own labels for notes and their places on notes (HAAL-102, D-109); card_assignee: the assignees of their cards (HAAL-119, D-97); link: links with an end the user reads — `container_kind`/`container_id` of the first end, `to_container_kind`/`to_container_id` of the second (HAAL-120, D-98); comment: the comments on their cards (HAAL-114, D-123); an item of kind card carries column_id, position, due_date, due_time |
| `entity_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `op` | string: `upsert`, `delete`, `tombstone` | yes | upsert carries the full resource (deleted_at included); tombstone = a container no longer readable (share revoked or left): remove it and everything in it |
| `version` | integer | yes |  |
| `data` | object |  | Full resource for upsert/delete; an item of kind event carries its event fields, a series also `exceptions` (excluded dates, YYYY-MM-DD, ascending); an item of kind note (HAAL-100 / D-87) carries pinned, archived_at, position, due_date, due_time (HH:MM, D-121), is_checklist — a note is its own container (container_kind note, container_id = its id) |

### Mutation

<a id="schema-mutation"></a>

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mutation_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `entity_type` | string: `calendar`, `item`, `reminder`, `checklist_item`, `board`, `board_column`, `label`, `item_label`, `card_assignee`, `link`, `comment` | yes | comment (HAAL-114, D-123): create `{item_id (a live card), body (Markdown, 1-10 000 characters, not only spaces)}` — the board owner or an edit share, not on an archived board, at most 1000 live comments per card; update `{body}` by its author only (403 otherwise; stamps edited_at); delete / restore (soft, one comment; the card's, its column's and its board's delete take its comments along) by its author or the board owner; a new comment tells the card's assignees except its author (notification `comment`). link (HAAL-120, D-98): create `{from_item_id, to_item_id, origin? (manual)}` — two different live events, notes or cards the user reads, at least one writable (owner or edit share, not archived): 403 otherwise; the same pair in either order: 409; itself: 422; at most 50 per item — delete / restore by whoever may write either end; an item’s delete leaves its links. card_assignee (HAAL-119, D-97): create `{item_id (a card), user_id (a member of its board: owner or an active share)}` (the same person twice: 409; not a member: 422; at most 20 per card), delete / restore — by the board owner or an edit share, not on an archived board; assigning someone else tells them (notification `assigned`). item of kind card (HAAL-112, D-92): create with `{kind: card, container_kind: board, container_id, column_id (a live, not archived column of the board), title (1-200 after trimming), position, body?, color?, priority?, due_date? (YYYY-MM-DD), due_time? (HH:MM, needs due_date)}`; update those fields (another column: column_id + position — the two merge as a pair, a conflict on one makes both a conflict, HAAL-113, D-93; clearing due_date clears due_time); a card cannot move to another board. label: create `{board_id, name (1-40, unique on the board, case ignored), color}`, update name and color, delete (takes it off every card in the same batch) / restore. item_label: create `{item_id (a card), label_id (a label of its board)}` (the same pair twice: 409), delete / restore. Board owner or edit share, not on an archived board. Personal labels for notes (HAAL-102, D-109): label create without `board_id` — the user's own label (unique among the user's labels, at most 100: 409), changed, deleted and restored by that user only; item_label create `{item_id (a live note the user reads, own or shared), label_id (the user's own label)}` (at most 20 of the user's labels on a note: 409), delete / restore by that user; nobody else sees either. board_column (HAAL-111, D-91): create with `{board_id (a live board), name (1-60 after trimming), position (fractional index), wip_limit? (1-999 or null), archived_at?}`; update name, position, wip_limit, archived_at (any timestamp archives, the server keeps its own time; null unarchives) — the board's owner or an edit share, not on an archived board (409); delete / restore (soft; a board's delete takes its columns along). board (HAAL-110, D-90): create with `{name (1-100 after trimming), position (fractional index, 1-64 letters or digits), archived_at?}`; update name, position, archived_at (any timestamp archives, the server keeps its own time; null unarchives) — the owner only; delete / restore (soft, the board with its content in one batch). An archived board is read-only: writes to its content are refused (409 invalid_state). reminder (HAAL-091): create with `{item_id, offset_minutes}` or `{item_id, all_day_time, all_day_days_before}` (events), or `{item_id, remind_at}` (notes: a date and time with its zone, fired once — HAAL-105, D-89), or one of the two event forms on a card with a due date (counted from its due date and time — HAAL-116, D-94); update the form fields; delete / restore (soft). checklist_item (HAAL-101, D-88): create with `{item_id (a live note), text (1-500 after trimming), position, checked?}` (at most 200 live items per note, else 409); update text, checked (the server stamps checked_at), position; delete / restore (soft, one item; the note's delete takes its items along) |
| `entity_id` | [Uuid](#schema-uuid) | yes |  |
| `op` | string: `create`, `update`, `delete`, `restore`, `move`, `exclude`, `include` | yes | exclude / include (item, a repeating event): data `{occurrence_date, override_event_id?}` — the date leaves the series (or is replaced by that one-off event in the same calendar) or comes back; the series version rises and its pulled data lists the excluded dates in `exceptions` |
| `base` | object |  | update / move: the values the client started from for each changed field (field-level merge, ADR-0009) |
| `base_version` | integer |  | Version the client edited (conflict detection); absent on create |
| `data` | object |  | create: the resource (calendar create: name, color — never the default, not archived; item create: kind `event`, container_kind `calendar`, container_id, title, body, color, priority and the event fields all_day, start_date, start_time, end_date, end_time (HH:MM), tzid (default: profile zone), location, rrule; copy_attachments_from — a duplicate (HAAL-096 / D-84) takes the live attachments of that event along when the user can read it, else none; or kind `note` (HAAL-100 / D-87): title (may be empty), body, color, priority, pinned, archived_at, is_checklist, position (required; fractional index, 1-64 letters or digits) — its own container, so container_kind / container_id are left out (or note / its own id); only its owner creates, reads and changes it until sharing of notes; a note cannot move); update: changed fields only — note: pinned, is_checklist, archived_at (any timestamp archives, the server keeps its own time; null unarchives; an archived note stays editable), position — calendar (owner, HAAL-094 / D-82): name, color, archived_at (any timestamp archives, the server keeps its own time; null unarchives; not the default calendar), is_default (only true: the default moves there; 409 for an archived calendar), and delete of the default calendar is refused (409); writes to items of an archived calendar are refused (409 invalid_state); event time fields conflict as a group; sets (labels, exceptions, assignees) as add/remove operations |
| `client_time` | [Timestamp](#schema-timestamp) |  |  |
